b1-n-gebuehr: To use the public toilet at the station, you must pay a small amount of money.
The bank takes a few euros each time you take cash from another bank's machine.
You must pay money to register your car at the office. The amount is set by the authorities.
b1-v-starten: The plane rolls down the runway and leaves the ground.
You turn the key and the engine of your car begins to run.
A company announces that its new service will begin next week.
b1-adj-virtuell: In a game you wear special glasses and walk around in a 3D world that does not really exist.
The team meets on a screen, with everybody at home. They never sit in the same room.
A shop exists only on the internet. You cannot visit it in real life.
b1-n-teil: A car repairman holds up a small broken piece of the engine.
You buy a cheap spare piece for your bike because the old one is worn out.
The manual lists every single small piece of the machine that you can replace.
b1-n-pille: The doctor gives you a small round tablet to swallow with water for your headache.
Every morning you swallow a tiny round vitamin with a glass of water.
At the pharmacy you ask for a small round medicine, not a liquid. Which word fits?
b1-v-aufheben: You drop a glove and bend down to take it from the floor.
The shop manager decides to end the old rule that nobody may bring a bag inside.
Keep your receipt and store it somewhere safe, you may need it later.
b1-n-rechner: At school, you press buttons on a small device to add big numbers quickly.
At the office, you sit at your desk and type on a keyboard in front of a screen.
The IT department says your machine is too old and needs to be replaced.
b1-n-politiker: A man stands on a stage before the election and gives speeches to get votes.
A man works in parliament and takes part in making the laws.
On the TV news, a man in a suit explains the new tax plan.
b1-adj-gleichzeitig: Two friends say the same word at the very same moment.
You cook dinner, talk on the phone and watch TV, all at once.
Two trains arrive at the platform at exactly the same time.
b1-v-vergroessern: You copy a small photo on a machine and make it much bigger.
The company builds a new hall to make the factory larger.
With a magnifying glass, you look at a tiny insect and it looks bigger.
b1-n-verdacht: The police believe the neighbour stole the bike, but they cannot prove it yet.
You see a stranger walking around your car again and again and you feel that something is wrong.
A shop owner thinks the boy took a sweet, but he has no proof.
b1-adv-hinunter: You walk from the top floor to the bottom. The stairs lead away from you to a lower place.
A ball rolls from the top of the hill to the bottom, away from you.
Which adverb means 'down' as a direction away from the speaker towards a lower place?
b1-n-umweltschutz: Volunteers pick up rubbish in the park and plant trees.
Your class collects bottles for recycling to help nature.
A group works to protect air, water and animals.
b1-n-flucht: A prisoner runs out of jail and gets away from the guards.
When fire breaks out, people run out of the building as fast as possible.
A thief gets away from the police on a motorbike.
b1-v-erfahren: You hear from your friend that she moved to Berlin.
A student finds out his exam result from an email.
You live in a foreign country for a year and go through many new things.
b1-adj-berufstaetig: The woman has a full job and goes to the office every day. She is in paid work.
On a form: 'Do you have a job at the moment?' You tick yes.
Many mothers have a paid job as well as raising their children.
b1-n-modell: At a fashion show, a woman walks along the stage and shows the new clothes.
A car company shows its newest version of the car.
An architect builds a small copy of the building from cardboard.
b1-n-mangel: In a hospital there are too few nurses.
After a dry summer, there is not enough water.
The product has a small flaw, a scratch, so you complain.
b1-v-uebertreiben: Your friend says: 'I waited a million hours!' but really it was ten minutes. He makes it sound bigger than it is.
You train too much at the gym and hurt yourself.
A salesman says the car is the best in the world. You think he is saying too much.
b1-n-strom: You plug in the kettle and turn on the lights. What makes the devices work?
A wide river flows slowly to the sea.
A bill from the energy company shows how much you used this month.
b1-n-verbot: A sign shows a red circle with a cigarette. Smoking is not allowed.
The city says no cars are allowed in the old town.
Your parents say you may not watch TV before homework.
b1-adj-schick: She wears a stylish dress and elegant shoes to the party.
A new restaurant has a smart, modern design.
He wears a fashionable jacket and everybody says he looks good.
b1-n-reportage: A TV programme shows what life is like in a fishing village, with interviews and pictures.
A magazine article describes from the scene how a big football match felt.
A journalist travels to a faraway city and writes a long, factual story about it.
b1-v-ausreichen: You have 10 euros and the ticket costs 8. Your money is enough.
Three eggs are enough for the cake.
One hour is enough to finish the work.
b1-n-schwiegersohn: Your daughter's husband comes to dinner.
A man talks about the man who married his daughter.
At the wedding, the father hugs the new husband of his daughter.
b1-n-rekord: The athlete runs faster than anybody has ever run before.
He swims the best result ever in this race.
A museum lists the tallest man who ever lived.
b1-v-veroeffentlichen: A writer finishes his book, and a company prints it and sells it.
A singer makes her new song available to everyone online.
b1-adv-sowieso: 'Shall I help you?' 'No thanks, I am going to the shop anyway.' Which adverb means 'in any case'?
You do not want to buy the jacket. It is too expensive anyway.
Why bother to ask? He will do what he wants in any case.
b1-n-vorort: Many people live outside the city centre in a quiet residential area and take the train to work.
The family moved from the centre to a green area at the edge of the city.
The bus goes from the main station to a district at the edge of the city.
b1-adj-gruendlich: The cleaner does not miss a single corner. He is careful and complete.
The doctor examines you carefully, step by step.
You check the text very carefully for mistakes.
b1-n-vertretung: The teacher is ill, so another teacher takes over. Today there is a 'cover' teacher.
A secretary is on holiday, and a temp does her work.
A company has an office in another country that speaks for the company there.
b1-v-schuetteln: You mix the juice by moving the bottle up and down quickly.
You say no without words by moving your head from side to side.
At a business meeting, you take someone's hand and move it up and down.
b1-n-technologie: The company develops new machines and computer programs. It is modern science used in practice.
Smartphones and robots are products of this field.
A university department studies how to use science to make new devices.
b1-n-affe: At the zoo, a hairy animal swings from branch to branch and eats a banana.
A child makes funny faces and jumps around. His mother says he is like this animal.
In the jungle, an animal with a long tail and hands climbs a tree.
b1-adj-aussen: The walls of the house are painted yellow on the side that faces the street.
The door handle on the side that faces the street is made of metal.
Which word means 'outside' as a position, 'on the ___ of the house'?
b1-n-galerie: You walk quietly through a room with paintings on the wall at an art exhibition.
A painter shows and sells his pictures in a small shop.
The new exhibition opens on Friday, with wine and photos.
b1-v-benoetigen: For a visa, you must have a valid passport and a photo.
'What do you need to bake a cake?' 'Flour, sugar and eggs.'
b1-n-verzeihung: You step on a stranger's foot and say sorry. Which word do you use?
A friend forgot your birthday and begs you not to be angry.
You bump into someone in the queue and say 'Excuse me!'
b1-n-organisation: A big group like the Red Cross helps people all over the world.
You arrange everything for the wedding: place, food and guests. All the planning is yours.
A charity is a group that works for a good cause without making money.
b1-v-verurteilen: The judge says the thief must pay a fine and gives him a punishment.
Everybody strongly says that the cruel act was wrong.
The court decides the driver is guilty and announces his punishment.
b1-n-aktion: The supermarket has special offers on milk this week.
Pupils organise a day to collect rubbish in the park.
A film with fights and explosions is full of this.
b1-adj-durchschnittlich: The test result was neither very good nor very bad. It was in the middle.
The mean temperature in July is 20 degrees, looking at all the days together.
An ordinary day with nothing special, neither great nor terrible.
b1-n-zahncreme: Every morning and night you put it on a brush and clean your teeth.
At the pharmacy you buy a tube with a mint taste for your teeth.
The dentist advises using one with fluoride.
b1-adv-moeglicherweise: You are not sure if it will rain tomorrow. You say it might.
A friend says he may come to the party, maybe.
The doctor says the pain could possibly come from stress.
b1-n-lautsprecher: You connect your phone to a box that plays your music loudly.
At the station, announcements come out of a device on the ceiling.
At a concert, huge black boxes on both sides of the stage make the sound loud.
b1-v-eroeffnen: A new restaurant starts business tomorrow at the street corner.
You go to the bank to start a new account.
The mayor cuts a ribbon to start the new bridge.
b1-n-mond: At night, a bright round shape in the sky lights the garden.
Astronauts first walked on it in 1969.
It changes shape from a thin curve to a full circle every month.
b1-adj-regional: The supermarket sells vegetables from farms in your area.
A newspaper reports only news from your own part of the country.
A dish is typical only in your part of the country.
b1-n-muelltonne: You throw your leftovers into a big plastic container outside the house.
On Thursdays, the rubbish truck empties the containers in front of the houses.
A big container on wheels stands at the kerb and is full of waste.
b1-v-stechen: A wasp attacks you on the arm with its small needle.
You push a needle into a balloon.
A mosquito bites you at night in summer.
b1-n-stau: On the motorway on Friday afternoon, the cars stand still for an hour.
You are late for work because of a long line of cars that is not moving.
The radio says: 'On the A9 there are 10 km of stop-and-go.'
b1-n-ersatz: Your phone breaks during the warranty and the shop gives you a new one.
The football player is injured, and another one comes on.
You lost the key, so you order a second one.
b1-v-achten: Cross the road carefully and look at the traffic.
You admire and honour your teacher.
A friend asks you to look at how much money you spend.
b1-n-denkmal: In the town square stands a large statue of a famous poet.
A tourist takes photos of a historic stone structure that remembers an event.
People put flowers at the memorial.
b1-adj-angenehm: It is a warm spring day with a soft breeze, and you feel good.
The sofa is soft and you sit on it comfortably.
The conversation with the new colleagues was friendly and nice.
b1-n-alarm: In a fire, a loud siren goes off in the building.
At 6 a.m. your phone makes a noise to wake you.
The shop's anti-theft system shouts when someone takes something without paying.
b1-n-kantine: At work at noon, you eat cheap lunch in a big room in the company building.
At school, students buy lunch at the place inside the school.
At the university, students line up for food in a big hall.
b1-v-vermuten: You see dark clouds and think it will probably rain.
Police think the thief is a local man but have no proof.
I suppose he is late because of traffic.
b1-n-speisewagen: On a long train trip, you go to a special carriage to eat a hot meal.
You are hungry between two cities and want a coffee while travelling on the train.
The ticket inspector says: 'Food is served in the carriage at the front.'
b1-n-halt: Our train makes a short one in Mainz. Some passengers get off.
You lose your grip and fall from the ladder. There was nothing to hold on to.
A climbing wall has small places where your fingers can find a grip.
b1-adv-normalerweise: You usually get up at 7, but today you got up at 9. Which adverb means 'as a rule'?
Which adverb means 'in the usual way'?
'Do you eat meat?' 'Usually, I eat vegetarian.'
b1-adj-aufmerksam: A pupil follows every word the teacher says and does not look away.
The waiter notices when your glass is empty.
A driver watches the road carefully.
b1-v-sich-anstrengen: Before the exam, you study hard and do not give up.
The runner pushes herself to win.
Your teacher says: 'Please give it your best.'
b1-n-wohnsitz: On the form, you must write the address where you officially live.
The tax office asks in which place you are registered to live.
A person has a main home in Berlin and a holiday house in Spain.
b1-n-unterhaltung: You sit with a friend and talk for an hour about the weekend.
A TV show with music and jokes after dinner is on, just for fun.
The hotel offers music, games and shows to amuse the guests.
b1-n-regel: A game: you must not touch the ball with your hands.
A sign at the pool says: 'No running.'
In class: 'Always raise your hand before speaking.'
b1-v-stammen: You ask where the tomatoes are from. 'They come from Spain.'
b1-adj-feucht: After rain the towel hangs outside and is a little wet but not dripping.
In the bathroom after a hot shower, the air is full of water.
The cloth is slightly wet and cool to touch.
b1-n-kuendigung: You tell your landlord in writing that you will leave the flat.
Your boss gives you a letter: your job will end next month.
You write to cancel your gym membership.
b1-n-steckdose: You need a place on the wall to plug in your phone charger.
A hotel room has only one in the whole room, near the bed.
An adapter fits in the wall hole to give you power.
b1-v-dekorieren: Before Christmas, you hang lights and balls on the tree.
Children put balloons and paper chains on the walls for a birthday.
A baker puts cream and fruit on top of a cake to make it pretty.
b1-n-abgas: Dirty fumes come out of the pipe at the back of the car.
Old diesel cars pollute the city air with what leaves their engine.
The technician checks the smoke that leaves your engine.
b1-n-gebirge: The Alps are a huge chain of high rocky hills with snow.
On holiday you drive through a range of tall peaks.
The weather report for the high land says it will snow.
b1-adj-individuell: Every student gets a lesson plan that fits his own needs.
You design a unique pair of shoes just for you.
Everyone has their own style, personal and not the same.
b1-v-verraten: You promised not to say anything about the surprise party, but you accidentally told the birthday girl.
A friend promised to stay loyal, but tells your secret to everyone and lets you down.
The look on her face showed that she was lying.
b1-n-puppe: A little girl plays with a toy that looks like a small person. She brushes its hair.
At the theatre, a toy figure with strings tells a story.
A shop window shows toys, among them a baby-shaped toy.
b1-n-langeweile: It rains all Sunday, and you have nothing to do. You feel this.
Children say: 'There is nothing to do!'
At a long, dull lecture, you look at the clock all the time.
b1-adv-jemals: 'Have you ___ been to Japan?' You ask if it happened at any time in your life.
'This is the best pizza I have ___ eaten.' Which adverb means 'ever'?
Which adverb means 'ever' in a question about your life?
b1-n-lexikon: In the library, a thick book explains words and topics in alphabetical order.
For a school project, you look up the topic 'volcano' in a big reference book.
A set of big books on the shelf explains many topics from A to Z.
b1-v-eilen: The bus arrives in two minutes, so you run quickly.
The doctor is called to an emergency and hurries there.
'We have time, so there is no need to rush.'
b1-n-video: You record a film of your birthday party with your phone.
On the internet, you watch a short moving clip about cats.
A tutorial shows how to repair a bike in moving pictures.
b1-adj-zusaetzlich: The hotel breakfast is included, but if you want a drink, you pay something more.
The teacher gives you more homework on top of the usual.
You buy a second ticket in addition to the first.
b1-n-moehre: A rabbit eats an orange vegetable that grows in the ground.
In a soup, there are orange pieces of vegetable.
Children say that if you eat a lot of this orange vegetable, you see better in the dark.
b1-v-erleben: On holiday in Iceland, you saw the northern lights. You went through something amazing.
He lived through a big storm in 1990 and tells about it.
'What did you go through on your trip?'
b1-n-atem: In winter you can see white clouds coming from your mouth.
After running up the stairs, you are almost out of this.
The doctor says: 'Breathe in, breathe out.' He listens to your air flow.
b1-n-einschreiben: You send an important contract and want the post office to give you proof of delivery.
A letter that the postman gives you only if you sign.
The tax office sends you a letter that you must sign for.
b1-adj-national: The football team plays for the whole country at the World Cup.
A park is protected for the whole country.
b1-n-gasthaus: In the village you eat schnitzel and drink beer in a traditional restaurant with rooms upstairs.
A small hotel stands by the road and has a bar.
A cosy old house with a bar where travellers sleep.
b1-v-messen: A tailor uses a tape to find out the length of your arm.
The doctor checks your body temperature.
You use a ruler to find the width of the table.
b1-n-streit: Two brothers shout at each other about who takes the last biscuit.
Neighbours keep fighting about the loud music.
A couple has a loud disagreement about money.
b1-n-sender: On the radio, you tune to a place that plays pop music.
A TV channel shows the news.
A tall tower sends the radio signals into the air.
b1-v-abonnieren: You pay each month to receive a magazine at home.
You press a button to see all the new videos of a YouTuber.
You sign up to get a newsletter by email every week.
b1-n-rat: Your friend asks what to do about a problem. You tell him your opinion.
In the town hall, a group of elected people decides local matters.
A grandmother says: 'My tip is to sleep on it.'
b1-adv-dahin: You hear about a beautiful beach and say you want to go to that place.
Show me the way: 'How do I get to that place?'
'Where are you going on Sunday?' 'To the lake, and you?' 'I would like to go to that place too.'
b1-adj-rechter: You write with your ___ hand, the one most people use.
In a car, the steering wheel is on the left and the passenger seat is on this side.
At the crossroads, you take the ___ lane. Which adjective is the opposite of 'left'?
b1-n-art: 'What kind of music do you like?'
Dogs are one type of animal. There are many types of dog.
'She talks in a friendly manner.' Which noun means 'way' or 'manner'?
b1-v-behaupten: A man says he saw the president but does not prove it.
A child strongly says he did not eat the cake, but there is chocolate on his face.
She says she is the best driver in the country.
b1-n-zutat: Flour, sugar and eggs are what you need for the cake. Each one is a single item in the recipe.
The label lists tomatoes, onion and salt.
The recipe has a list headed with what you need to buy and mix.
b1-n-aussprache: Your teacher repeats a word because you say it wrongly. It is about how it sounds.
A dictionary shows symbols to tell how words sound.
You practise saying difficult words aloud.
b1-n-droge: A police poster says: 'Say no to illegal substances like cocaine.'
A doctor warns about substances that harm your body and make you dependent.
A young man is in trouble because he took substances that are not allowed.
